title: Etaleness near a regular coordinate fibre
statement: Let p:X→S be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] and i:Y→X a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let a,b≥0, h:X→A^(a+b)_S over S, and v:Y→A^a_S etale [def-sbc-affine-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Assume the square formed by v,i,h and the inclusion setting the last b coordinates to zero is cartesian [def-pc-base-change]. Assume on every affine open of X the pullbacks of those b coordinates are weakly regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Then for each y∈Y there is an open neighbourhood T of i(y) such that h restricted to T is etale. This is a criterion for a specified map h; no coordinates are constructed.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, last two proof paragraphs: finite presentation, fibre dimension comparison, miracle flatness, fibre criterion and etale criterion

proof.text: Affine-space projection q is smooth. Finite-presentation permanence applied to h≫q=p makes h locally of finite presentation. The cartesian square identifies v with the base change of h along the zero-coordinate inclusion. The unramified-locus base-change theorem therefore puts i(y) in the unramified locus of h, since v is etale. Its unramified neighbourhood gives a formally unramified actual stalk map h_(i(y))^# by cancellation of the open-immersion stalk isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, finite presentation and etale base change; morphisms.tex Tag 02GF

proof.text: Put s=p(i(y)), z=p.asFiber(i(y)) and let m:X_s→(A^(a+b)_S)_s be the canonical pullback map. Apply the regular-coordinate fibre dimension formula to m at z. Both its local rings are regular local, since p and q have smooth fibres over the residue field of s. A minimal generating family of the target-ring maximal ideal has length its Krull dimension and is a regular sequence. The defining supremum for depth gives depth at least that dimension. Miracle flatness now makes m_z^# flat.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, final paragraph; algebra.tex Tags 00NQ and 00R4

proof.text: The pointwise fibrewise flatness criterion applies to p,q,h at i(y): p is locally finitely presented and flat at that point by smoothness; q is locally of finite type; and the actual map on base-fibre stalks is flat by the previous step. It yields flatness of h_(i(y))^#.

Choose affine target and source neighbourhoods of h(i(y)) and i(y). The affine stalk-map arrow isomorphism transports flatness and formal unramifiedness to the prime localizations. Compose formal unramifiedness with the base localization, and use localization of differentials to see that the localized differential module vanishes. The etale-at-prime criterion then gives a basic localization of the source algebra that is etale over the target algebra. Its corresponding affine basic open contains i(y). The affine property comparison and the target open immersion turn this into Etale(T.ι≫h).

theorem Scheme.Hom.exists_etale_open_of_regular_coordinate_fibre
    {S X Y : Scheme.{u}} (p : X ⟶ S) [Smooth p] (i : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (a b : ℕ)
    (h : X ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S)
    (v : Y ⟶ AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S) [Etale v]
    (hh : h ≫ (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin (a + b))) S ↘ S) = p)
    (H : IsPullback v i
      (AffineSpace.homOfVector (AffineSpace (ULift.{u} (Fin a)) S ↘ S)
        (fun j ↦ Fin.addCases (fun k ↦ AffineSpace.coord S (ULift.up k))
          (fun _ ↦ 0) j.down)) h)
    (hreg : ∀ W : X.affineOpens,
      RingTheory.Sequence.IsWeaklyRegular Γ(X, W)
        (List.ofFn (fun j : Fin b ↦
          X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (le_top : W.1 ≤ ⊤)).op
            (h.appTop (AffineSpace.coord S (ULift.up (Fin.natAdd a j)))))))
    (y : Y) :
    ∃ T : X.Opens, i y ∈ T ∧ Etale (T.ι ≫ h)
